reason: Plan Phase 5, the shadow behind the gauge. The layering research: main+0xa494a0 appends (0,node) on entry and (1,node) on exit in visit order and consumes that list in order (vtable 0x38/0x3c on kind 0, 0x40 on kind 1, return on kind 2), with no sort and no z value - paint order is walk order. The GUI resource's Priority property (hud0: Txt_sharp 0, Txt_sharpefx 1, Txt_sharpEdge 2; setter main+0xa47a04, getter main+0xa479fc, the word pair +0x5c/+0x60 propagated to the parent) ordered that chain when the row was built; the walker never reads it, so a node inserted at runtime gets its layer from its link. So r54 links root.child = shadow with shadow.sibling = mask: the walker emits the shadow's pair before the mask's enter record, the shadow draws under the gauge and outside the scissor, the bar's ink covers its kept part and the sprite's own shape shows past the cut. The shadow keeps the bar's own position pair and authored 88 x 24 from the build, so the per-frame quad writes and the authored/position unit conversion (core's dim_quad) are deleted; the only per-frame write left is the atlas band at +0x10c following the bar's live tier band, which lands one frame late. Colour #202326 = 0xFF262320 (alpha, blue, green, red, proven by the r52 run). Storage unchanged: 5 tree nodes, 6-word array, 88 bytes = 11 records; the tree fixture pins kinds 0,1,0,0,1,0,1,0,1,1,2 with the shadow's pair first and the mask's exit closing the scissor scope. r44's accepted cut is unchanged. **r53 - the shadow carved to the hidden part in the gauge's band, drawn on top - is kept unchanged at build/modern-sharpness-gauge/candidates/r53/ as the fallback if the behind version shows a dark rim on the kept side.** 21 host fixtures pass; verify PASSED with 33 signature windows.
runtime_test: The accepted cut is r44's, accepted on its Eden run of 2026-10-30. r52 ran on Eden 2026-10-31: the copy is on screen as a full-length magenta blade under the sharpness gauge, and it stays in place as sharpness decreases and increases and across areas (the tester's photo work/modern-sharpness-gauge/visual/r52/r52-magenta-photo.webp, sha256 a6fc2f82b722d66c76642666b4e47e1b17c76841148d993f10bce31453e4e638; the log was not retained). Earlier Phase 5 attempts on Eden 2026-10-31: r45 froze the game; r46 refused its copy at stage 52; r47, r48 and r50 ran clean with the copy in the tree and none of it visible, their dim_flags=0x20a0001 being the constructor's default. r53 and r54 have not been run.

limitations: the shadow's look behind the gauge, unmeasured: it shows through the bar art's semi-transparent pixels, so a dark rim along the blade's outline and under its bloom on the kept side is expected. r53 (the shadow carved to the hidden part, in the band, on top) is preserved at build/modern-sharpness-gauge/candidates/r53/ as the fallback if that is unwanted

the atlas band follows the bar's tier one frame late, because it is written at the mask's enter, which the walk visits after the shadow's records; the fix is a hook at the shadow's own enter (this class's vtable slot 0x38, main+0x85628), gated on the marker word, and it is not built
r4 has no runtime test; its lines, the 320-sample budget and the absence of any drawing change are static results.
r2 was built and never run; r3 was run once on Eden and is recorded.
r14 was run once on Eden and failed as reported: the gauge was clipped away from the insertion and the game crashed at the quest end. Its log is the evidence, and the insertion is removed in r15.

r15 was run once on Eden and drew the gauge normally for 740 seconds with no exception; its facts line printed tree_nodes 3 against 4 objects, and its object-list fields were read from the wrong object (the controller's owner field), which is what r16 fixes.

r16 changes nothing on screen: it reads game memory and logs. No drawing, no gauge change, and no cleanup claim (the root-destructor hook fired zero times in the three sessions that logged it). Its Eden run ended in Eden's own shutdown records (maxwell_3d Critical asserts, ForceStop, host SIGSEGV) with zero guest exceptions.
the game's destructor is assumed to free the map block r17 publishes through the cGUIInstance DTI's MT allocator; that free has not been observed, and r17 frees the old 4-word block itself
The per-weapon tier tables live in RomFS weapon data and are not read in this workspace: no weapon data file is extracted here.
The gauge itself is not part of r4.

r25 has not been run. r24's run drew the gauge from the quest start and lost it at an area change, where a mask kept clipping after its links broke; the disable-on-loss path has no runtime evidence, and a mask inserted into a second area's row has never been observed (r24's log ends 12 s after the transition, gauge HUD absent)
r40 has not been run. Its two defaults are the endpoints the r39 log shows applied (right edge 129 px at 0% and 201 px at 100%), read from the tester's run, not from an r40 run.
r42 has not been run. Its fill comes from the player fields Phase 1 verified and the r41 run's accepted geometry; the per-frame fill has not been seen on screen.
r43 has not been run. 128 px at 0% is proven by the r42 log (the tester dragged the start there); 200 px at 100% is the tester's measurement, and that run's box ended at 201.
The thread that runs the draw walker at main+0xa494a0 is unproven, and the run did not change that: no bl site, stored word or DTI property in main names that entry.

The MT `color` word's byte order is unproven, so the dim blade's alpha byte position is an inference. The facts line now prints the bar's four corner colours, so a run pins it next to the colour on screen.

The r44 release bytes are preserved in backups/accepted/modern-sharpness-gauge/r44-before-dim-empty-blade/, runtime UNCHANGED; r45 through r52 are superseded, r52 with its copy seen on screen; r53 is a new candidate and carries no distribution approval.
